【P1｜Mr. Utterson】
别称：Utterson
当前一句话身份：Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
档案（最新）：occupation：lawyer；personality：blameless past, troubled by old sins；situation：obsessed with finding and seeing Hyde；residence：bachelor house near a church；identity：lawyer of Gaunt Street
关系：Mr. Richard Enfield（cousin）、Dr. Jekyll（old friend）、Dr. Lanyon（friend）
至今经历（按时间）：
- Enfield points his cane at a sinister door and asks Utterson if he ever remarked it.
- Enfield calls the door place Black Mail House and muses.
- Utterson asks the name of the man who walked over the child.
- Utterson says he already knows the other party's name.
- Enfield and Utterson agree never to refer to the matter again.
- Utterson comes home in low spirits and studies Jekyll's will in his business room.
- The will leaves all Jekyll's possessions to Edward Hyde, and Hyde inherits if Jekyll vanishes.
- Utterson calls the will madness and now fears it is disgrace.
- Utterson goes to Cavendish Square to consult his friend Dr. Lanyon.
- Lanyon welcomes Utterson warmly as an old school and college friend.
- Utterson asks whether he and Lanyon are Jekyll's two oldest friends.
- Utterson asks Lanyon about Hyde, and Lanyon has never heard of him.
- Utterson lies awake all night, haunted by Enfield's tale and the faceless figure.
- Utterson keeps watch by the by-street door at all hours until his patience is rewarded.
- Utterson resolves to hunt for Hyde, thinking 'If he be Mr. Hyde, I shall be Mr. Seek.'
- A small plainly dressed man approaches the door with a key, and Utterson accosts him as Mr. Hyde.
- Utterson accosts Hyde and asks to be admitted to see Jekyll.
- Utterson asks to see Hyde's face and studies it.
- Hyde angrily accuses Utterson of lying about Jekyll's description.
- Utterson walks away deeply disturbed by Hyde's appearance.
- Utterson arrives at Jekyll's house and is admitted by Poole.
- Poole tells Utterson that Dr. Jekyll has gone out.
- Poole confirms Hyde has a key and comes by the dissecting room door.
- Poole says all servants have orders to obey Hyde.
- Poole says Hyde never dines there and mostly uses the laboratory.
- Utterson goes home fearing Jekyll is in deep waters.

[note_g1]
Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield。Mr. Utterson is a lawyer of Gaunt Street, kinsman and friend of Richard Enfield, and old friend of Dr. Jekyll and Dr. Lanyon. He is a man of blameless past, troubled by old sins. Enfield showed him a sinister door and told of a man who trampled a child. Utterson studied Jekyll's will, which leaves everything to Edward Hyde. He consulted Lanyon, who had never heard of Hyde. Utterson kept watch by the by-street door until he accosted Hyde, studied his face, and was deeply disturbed. He then learned from Poole that Jekyll was out and that Hyde had a key. He now fears Jekyll is in deep waters.

[note_g2]
Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque。Edward Hyde is a small, plainly dressed man with a husky, whispering, broken voice, known as Jekyll's friend and benefactor, living in Soho. He is merciless and inspires enduring hatred. He trampled a girl and paid a hundred pounds with a cheque from Jekyll's account. Jekyll's will names him heir if Jekyll vanishes. Utterson accosted him at the by-street door; Hyde gave his Soho address, accused Utterson of lying about Jekyll, then unlocked the door and disappeared. He has a key to Jekyll's house, comes by the dissecting room door, and all servants are ordered to obey him. He now mostly uses the laboratory and never dines there.

[note_g3]
Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor。Dr. Lanyon is a doctor with a house in Cavendish Square, an old school and college friend of Mr. Utterson and a friend of Dr. Jekyll. He is hearty, red-faced, prematurely white-haired, boisterous, decided, theatrical but genuine. Utterson came to consult him about Jekyll's will and Hyde. Lanyon welcomed him warmly, said Jekyll had become too fanciful and wrong in mind over ten years ago, and had never heard of Hyde. He now remains Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor, unaware of Hyde's identity.

[note_g4]
Elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house。Poole is the elderly servant and butler at Dr. Jekyll's house, serving his master Dr. Jekyll and obeying the man in the middle as an obeyed superior. He admitted Utterson to Jekyll's house and told him Jekyll had gone out. He confirmed that Hyde has a key and comes by the dissecting room door, that all servants have orders to obey Hyde, and that Hyde never dines there and mostly uses the laboratory. He now continues in his post, bound by orders to obey Hyde.

[note_g5]
